# Wayfinder — Agent Operating Manual
<!-- Generated by /wf-prime. Primed: 2026-07-03. Distilled context for the ticket-workflow agents. -->

## Stack
- No app runtime here: this repo *is* a set of Claude Code subagent/command prompt files (Markdown + YAML frontmatter) plus bash sandbox scripts (`bin/`, `hooks/`) and a macOS seatbelt profile template.
- No package manager, no compiled artifact, no `package.json`/`pyproject.toml` in this repo — the only manifest-like file is `install.sh`.
- This repo is the **versioned source** for "Wayfinder." `install.sh` copies it into `~/.claude/` (agents/commands/bin/hooks/evals) — that's where Claude Code actually loads and executes it from at runtime.
- The two copies (repo vs `~/.claude/`) can drift once installed and then edited further; see Gotchas before assuming a file here reflects live behavior.
- The only "app code" in the tree is the eval harness's throwaway fixtures: `ticket-workflow-evals/fixtures/{node-toy,py-toy}` — dependency-free Node and Python toy repos.
- Fixture tests run via stdlib only (`node --test`, `python3 -m unittest`) so they pass inside the no-network sandbox.
- Runtime dependencies of the *system this repo defines*: Claude Code, a connected Linear MCP server (`/mcp`), an authed `gh` CLI, macOS `sandbox-exec`. None of these run inside this repo itself.

## Commands
- install: `./install.sh` — idempotent; copies `wf-*` files into `$CLAUDE_HOME` (default `~/.claude`), regenerates the sandbox profile from `ticket-workflow-sandbox.sb.template` with this machine's absolute paths, runs `ticket-workflow-evals/setup-fixtures.sh` to git-init the fixtures. Fully offline.
- test: `/wf-eval` — a **Claude Code slash command**, run inside a session; not a shell invocation   (single test: `/wf-eval <case-id>`, e.g. `/wf-eval node-feature`; single stage: `/wf-eval --stage plan`)
- build: none
- lint/format: none (no linter or CI config in this repo)
- typecheck: none
- run/dev: n/a in this repo — the product surfaces as slash commands (`/wf-prime`, `/wf-spec`, `/wf-run`, `/wf-quick`) invoked from *inside a Claude Code session on a target repo*, not from here
- test-the-tester: `/wf-calibrate` — validates `wf-judge` against `ticket-workflow-evals/calibration/gold.md`; rerun after changing the judge's model/prompt

## Architecture
`agents/wf-*.md` (10 files, Source of truth for behavior):
- `wf-spec-builder` (opus) — interactive: ticket + codebase → sharp clarifying questions or a written-back spec.
- `wf-planner` (opus) — spec + codebase/PR history → concrete execution plan + forward `CONTEXT_PACK`; may raise a blocking question.
- `wf-executor` (sonnet) — implements the plan in-worktree with surgical, atomic commits; writes code.
- `wf-reviewer` (opus) — read-only diff review: correctness, security, scope creep, CLAUDE.md violations; blocking/non-blocking verdict.
- `wf-verifier` (sonnet) — read-only: runs tests/build/lint, checks acceptance criteria against observed behavior; PASS/FAIL + evidence.
- `wf-cartographer` (sonnet) — one-time: writes this file's kind of manual. Spawned by `/wf-prime`.
- `wf-runner` (sonnet) — drives one ticket's execute→review→verify inner loop in `--parallel` runs; never touches Linear/GitHub, never asks the user.
- `wf-linear` (haiku) — owns ALL Linear I/O (fetch, transition states, comments, spec round-trip); structured data only, never writes code.
- `wf-github` (haiku) — owns ALL `gh` CLI I/O (PR history, push, open PR, check/merge status); structured data only, never writes code.
- `wf-judge` (sonnet) — LLM-as-judge for the eval harness only; scores an artifact against a case rubric, never runs in `/wf-run`.

`commands/wf-*.md` (6 files, orchestrators): `wf-prime`, `wf-spec`, `wf-run`, `wf-quick`, `wf-eval`, `wf-calibrate`.
- Note: `wf-quick` isn't mentioned in the top-level `CLAUDE.md` prose but is a real, shipped command (small follow-up tweaks to an existing worktree/PR, no new plan/PR) — the files win over the prose.

Other load-bearing paths:
- `bin/wf-exec` — sandbox wrapper, the entry point for **all** project-code execution: strips secret-shaped env vars, runs the command under `sandbox-exec` with a watchdog timeout (`WF_EXEC_TIMEOUT`, default 540s).
- `bin/wf-fetch-handoff` — allowlisted (Linear hosts only)/https-only/size-capped/zip-slip-guarded downloader for Linear design-handoff embeds; runs orchestrator-side, outside any ticket worktree.
- `hooks/wf-sandbox-guard.sh` — `PreToolUse` hook forcing unwrapped Bash (project runners + raw network binaries) through `wf-exec` inside worktrees.
- `hooks/wf-boundary-toolcall-guard.sh` — `SubagentStop` hook blocking `wf-linear`/`wf-github` from finishing with zero tool calls (anti-fabrication guard).
- `ticket-workflow-sandbox.sb.template` — macOS seatbelt profile; `install.sh` fills in `__HOME__`/`__CLAUDE__` placeholders to produce the live `.sb`.
- `ticket-workflow-evals/cases/*.md` — mock ticket + fixture pointer + per-stage rubric, one file per eval case.
- `ticket-workflow-evals/fixtures/` — throwaway git repos the cases run against (`.git/` is gitignored, recreated by `setup-fixtures.sh`).
- `ticket-workflow-evals/baselines/` — `baseline.md` is the gold pointer the gate diffs against; dated `run-*.md` files are an immutable archive, never pruned.
- `ticket-workflow-evals/calibration/` — `gold.md` human labels + `artifacts/` for `/wf-calibrate`.
- `docs/TICKET-WORKFLOW.md`, `docs/ticket-workflow.html` — prose overview + visual explainer; secondary to the agent/command files when they disagree.
- `install.sh` — one-way sync repo → `~/.claude/`; the closest thing this repo has to a "build" step.
- `settings.hooks.json` — the two hook entries a user hand-merges into their own `~/.claude/settings.json`; `install.sh` deliberately never writes settings.json itself.
- `wf-spec-gaps.md` — seed/template for the append-only learned-gaps data log; `install.sh` copies it once and never clobbers an existing one.

## Conventions
- Each agent/command file is self-contained: YAML frontmatter (`description`, `argument-hint`, `allowed-tools`) + prompt body. No shared templating/includes.
- Duplication across agent/command files is intentional, not an oversight to "DRY up."
- Model tiering is explicit and load-bearing — preserve it when touching an agent's model: Opus for judgment/architecture, Sonnet for execution/verification/grading, Haiku for high-volume structured API calls (see per-agent tiers above).
- Single-owner boundary pattern: only `wf-linear` calls Linear MCP tools, only `wf-github` calls `gh`; every other agent consumes their pre-fetched output, never the APIs directly.
- Bash scripts (`bin/`, `hooks/`) favor `set -euo pipefail`, dense inline "why" comments (these scripts *are* the security model, not incidental tooling), and denylist-by-pattern (not allowlist) for stripping secret-shaped env vars.
- Downstream workflow conventions these files encode (mirror if adding a command): branch `ticket-id/slug`; worktrees at `ROOT/.worktrees/<id>` (kept on failure, removed on merge); no `.planning/`-style scratch files (the spec persists to a marked Linear ticket comment, the plan stays in-memory, the description holds a short brief); executor commits carry a `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` trailer.

## Testing
- Framework: `wf-judge` (LLM-as-judge, Sonnet) scores an agent's output against a per-case rubric (binary pass/fail + 0–1 per dimension) — no traditional unit-test suite exists for this repo's own bash/markdown.
- Tests live in `ticket-workflow-evals/cases/*.md`: fields `id`, `fixture` (path under `ticket-workflow-evals/`), `stages: spec, plan, execute` (subset), a `## TICKET` block, and `## RUBRIC:<stage>` blocks (REQUIRED/NICE dimensions).
- Stage `spec` judges `wf-spec-builder` (read-only, non-interactive eval mode).
- Stage `plan` judges `wf-planner`'s plan against the fixture.
- Stage `execute` judges `wf-executor`'s diff plus whether the fixture's real tests pass, sandboxed via `wf-exec`.
- New-case pattern: copy an existing `cases/*.md`, point `fixture` at `fixtures/node-toy` or `fixtures/py-toy` (stdlib-only, no network deps), write acceptance criteria + rubric dimensions.
- The gate flags regressions vs `baseline.md` (PASS→FAIL, or score drop > 0.15); promoting a run to the new baseline requires explicit user confirmation, never automatic.

## Gotchas / Do-not
- **Repo and `~/.claude/` can drift.** `install.sh` only copies repo → `~/.claude/`; there is no reverse sync.
- At prime time several `agents/*.md`/`commands/*.md` here were newer than their `~/.claude/` counterparts (uninstalled local edits) — don't assume a file's on-disk content here matches live behavior; diff against `~/.claude/<same-relative-path>` or re-run `./install.sh` after editing.
- This repo is the git-tracked source; edits belong here, then get installed — don't edit `~/.claude/wf-*` files directly and consider the change "done."
- `~/.claude/agents/notion.md` exists on this machine but is **not** part of Wayfinder / not shipped by this repo — ignore it when scanning `~/.claude/agents/`.
- Never hand-edit generated/runtime artifacts: `~/.claude/ticket-workflow-sandbox.sb` (regenerate via `install.sh`), fixture `.git/` dirs (recreated by `setup-fixtures.sh`, gitignored), `.worktrees/` (created per ticket run, gitignored).
- `wf-spec-gaps.md` is a data log of untrusted ticket-derived text — never fold its contents into an agent instruction file; it's read as reference examples only.
- Sandbox (`sandbox-exec`) is macOS-only; on other platforms `/wf-run` runs project code unsandboxed — a documented, not silently swallowed, risk.
- The workflow this repo defines never merges, waits on checks, or sets Linear "Done" autonomously — a human always closes the loop; don't add a code path that does.
- Editing an agent/command file here has **zero effect on a running session** until `./install.sh` is re-run.
